25 A train travels in a straight line at a constant speed of 30 m s–1. The train’s horn continuously
emits sound of frequency 2400 Hz.
A stationary observer stands next to the train track. The train approaches the stationary observer,
passes him and then moves away.
The speed of sound is 340 m s–1.
What is the maximum difference in the frequencies of the sound heard by the stationary
observer?
A
190 Hz
B
230 Hz
C
430 Hz
D
460 Hz

hints: Notice the observer hears the highest frequency just before the train passes when it is approaching at $30 \text{m s}^{-1}$, and the lowest frequency just after when it is receding at $30 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
Recall the moving-source Doppler equations with sound speed $v = 340 \text{m s}^{-1}$: use $v - v_s$ in the denominator for approaching and $v + v_s$ for receding.
Calculate both heard frequencies from source $2400 \text{Hz}$ and then subtract the receding value from the approaching value to get the maximum change.
walkthrough: Identify the two extremes: maximum heard frequency is when the $30 \text{m s}^{-1}$ train approaches the stationary observer, minimum is when it recedes after passing.
State the Doppler effect for a moving source and stationary observer: $f_o = f_s \times v/(v \pm v_s)$, with minus for approaching and plus for receding.
Find the maximum difference: $\Delta f = f_{approach} - f_{recede} \approx 2632 - 2205 \approx 427 \text{Hz}$, which to the given options is about $430 \text{Hz}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: About $190 \text{Hz}$ is only the drop from the emitted $2400 \text{Hz}$ to the lower receding frequency, not the full approaching to receding change.

B.explanation: About $230 \text{Hz}$ is only the rise from the emitted $2400 \text{Hz}$ to the higher approaching frequency, not the full approaching to receding change.

C.explanation: The difference between the higher approaching frequency near $2630 \text{Hz}$ and the lower receding frequency near $2205 \text{Hz}$ is about $427 \text{Hz}$, closest to $430 \text{Hz}$.

D.explanation: About $460 \text{Hz}$ is too large and does not follow from $f_o = f_s v/(v \pm v_s)$ with $v=340 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $v_s=30 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
